mcq.q: NITI Aayog, which replaced the Planning Commission, came into existence on:
mcq.explain: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was set up on 1 January 2015 to replace the Planning Commission, which had been established in March 1950. The Prime Minister is its Chairperson. It acts as a policy think tank and promotes cooperative federalism.
mcq.topic: NITI Aayog

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT a function of NITI Aayog?
options: Acting as a policy think tank for the government
mcq.explain: Unlike the old Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not allocate funds to States or ministries; transfers are now governed by the Finance Commission and the Finance Ministry. NITI Aayog serves as a think tank, encourages cooperative and competitive federalism, and monitors and evaluates programmes.
mcq.topic: NITI Aayog
mcq.fast: NITI Aayog advises; it does not hand out money.

mcq.q: The "drain of wealth" theory, explaining how colonial rule transferred India's resources to Britain, is associated with:
mcq.explain: Dadabhai Naoroji, in his writings including "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India", argued that a large part of India's wealth was being drained to Britain through home charges, salaries and pensions of British officials, and profits, without any return. This became a central idea of economic nationalism.
mcq.topic: Pre-colonial prosperity and the colonial economy (1757–1947)

mcq.q: The Permanent Settlement, which fixed land revenue permanently with zamindars in Bengal, was introduced in 1793 by:
mcq.explain: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in 1793 in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. Zamindars became owners of land and paid a fixed revenue to the Company. Since their payment was fixed, they often squeezed the cultivators, while investment in agriculture remained poor.
mcq.topic: Pre-colonial prosperity and the colonial economy (1757–1947)

mcq.q: The first passenger railway line in India (1853) ran between:
mcq.explain: India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853 from Bombay (Bori Bunder) to Thane. Railways under colonial rule were built mainly to move raw materials to ports and British manufactures inland, though they also helped integrate markets and move people across the country.
mcq.topic: Pre-colonial prosperity and the colonial economy (1757–1947)

mcq.q: The Second Five Year Plan (1956–61), based on the Mahalanobis model, emphasised:
options: Rapid industrialisation with priority to heavy and basic industries
mcq.explain: The Second Plan, built on P. C. Mahalanobis's model, gave priority to heavy and basic industries such as steel, machinery and power, with a leading role for the public sector. The First Plan had emphasised agriculture and irrigation. Privatisation came only after 1991.
mcq.topic: Post-independence strategy (1947–1991): planning, public sector, licence raj

mcq.q: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 classified industries into three schedules. Schedule A industries were:
options: To be developed exclusively by the State
mcq.explain: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 placed industries such as arms, atomic energy, iron and steel and railways in Schedule A, whose future development was the exclusive responsibility of the State. Schedule B industries were to be progressively State-owned with private participation, and Schedule C was left to the private sector.
mcq.topic: Post-independence strategy (1947–1991): planning, public sector, licence raj

mcq.q: In 1980, how many more commercial banks were nationalised in India?
mcq.explain: Fourteen major commercial banks were nationalised in July 1969, and six more were nationalised in April 1980. The aim was to spread banking to rural areas and direct credit towards priority sectors such as agriculture and small industry.
mcq.topic: Post-independence strategy (1947–1991): planning, public sector, licence raj

mcq.q: The Green Revolution in India in the mid-1960s was most successful in:
options: Wheat, especially in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
mcq.explain: The Green Revolution used high-yielding variety seeds with assured irrigation, fertilisers and pesticides. Its biggest success was in wheat, in irrigated regions such as Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. Pulses, coarse cereals and rain-fed regions gained much less, which increased regional inequality.
mcq.topic: The Green Revolution

mcq.q: The Indian agricultural scientist most closely associated with the Green Revolution is:
mcq.explain: M. S. Swaminathan played the leading role in introducing and adapting high-yielding wheat varieties in India in the 1960s, working with Norman Borlaug's varieties. Verghese Kurien led the White Revolution (Operation Flood) in milk, while Raman and Bhabha were physicists.
mcq.topic: The Green Revolution

mcq.q: Which Act replaced the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) as part of the reforms?
mcq.explain: The Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999 replaced the restrictive FERA of 1973. FEMA treats foreign exchange violations as civil matters rather than criminal offences and aims to facilitate external trade and payments. The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the MRTP Act.
mcq.topic: The 1991 crisis and the reform package (LPG)

mcq.q: The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act was replaced by:
mcq.explain: The MRTP Act, 1969 focused on controlling the size of large business houses. It was replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, which focuses instead on preventing anti-competitive agreements and abuse of dominance and regulating combinations, enforced by the Competition Commission of India.
mcq.topic: The 1991 crisis and the reform package (LPG)

mcq.q: At the time of the 1991 reforms, the Prime Minister and the Finance Minister of India were respectively:
options: Rajiv Gandhi and V. P. Singh
Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Yashwant Sinha
P. V. Narasimha Rao and Dr Manmohan Singh
mcq.explain: The New Economic Policy of 1991 was launched by the government of Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao, with Dr Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister. Its liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation measures responded to the balance of payments crisis of that year.
mcq.topic: The 1991 crisis and the reform package (LPG)

mcq.q: The letters "LPG" in the context of the 1991 reforms stand for:
mcq.explain: The 1991 reforms are summed up as LPG: liberalisation (removing licences and controls), privatisation (reducing the role of the public sector, including disinvestment) and globalisation (integrating with the world economy through lower tariffs and more foreign investment).
mcq.topic: The 1991 crisis and the reform package (LPG)

mcq.q: Sale of part of the government's shareholding in public sector enterprises is called:
mcq.explain: Disinvestment means the government selling part or all of its equity in public sector enterprises to private investors or the public. It raises resources for the government and aims to improve efficiency. Nationalisation is the opposite — the State taking over private enterprises.
mcq.topic: The 1991 crisis and the reform package (LPG)

mcq.q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India with effect from:
mcq.explain: GST came into force on 1 July 2017, following the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016. It replaced many Central and State indirect taxes with a single destination-based tax, creating a more unified national market. 8 November 2016 was the date of demonetisation.
mcq.topic: Outcomes of three decades of reform

mcq.q: On 8 November 2016, the Government of India withdrew the legal tender status of:
mcq.explain: On 8 November 2016 the Government announced the demonetisation of the then existing ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes, which formed the bulk of currency in circulation by value. The stated aims included fighting black money, counterfeit currency and terror financing, and promoting digital payments.
mcq.topic: Outcomes of three decades of reform

mcq.q: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, which provides a time-bound process for resolving stressed companies, was enacted in:
mcq.explain: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code was enacted in 2016 to consolidate insolvency laws and provide a time-bound resolution process for companies, partnerships and individuals. It created the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India and gave creditors control during resolution.
mcq.topic: Outcomes of three decades of reform

mcq.q: Which sector contributes the largest share of India's Gross Value Added today?
mcq.explain: Since the 1990s, the services sector — trade, transport, finance, IT, real estate, public administration and others — has become the largest contributor to India's GVA, accounting for more than half. Agriculture's share has fallen steadily, even though it still employs the largest share of workers.
mcq.topic: Current state — tertiary sector (services) and conclusion
mcq.fast: Largest GVA share = services; largest employer = agriculture.

mcq.q: Which sector still employs the largest share of India's workforce?
mcq.explain: Although its share in GVA has fallen to under a fifth, agriculture and allied activities still employ the largest share of India's workforce. This mismatch means output per worker in agriculture is low, which is why moving workers to more productive sectors is a key development challenge.
mcq.topic: Current state — primary sector (agriculture)
mcq.fast: Agriculture: small share of output, biggest share of jobs.

mcq.q: The "Make in India" initiative to promote manufacturing and investment was launched in:
mcq.explain: The Make in India initiative was launched in September 2014 to encourage companies to manufacture in India, attract investment, build infrastructure and improve the ease of doing business. Later schemes such as Production Linked Incentives (from 2020) built on it.
mcq.topic: Current state — secondary sector (industry)

mcq.q: The decline of traditional Indian handicrafts under colonial rule, as cheap machine-made British goods flooded the market, is called:
mcq.explain: Under British rule, traditional Indian industries such as handloom weaving declined sharply, because of competition from cheap machine-made British goods, discriminatory tariffs and the loss of royal patronage. Artisans were pushed into agriculture, increasing pressure on land. This process is called deindustrialisation.
mcq.topic: Pre-colonial prosperity and the colonial economy (1757–1947)
mcq.fast: Handicrafts destroyed under colonial rule = deindustrialisation.

mcq.q: The White Revolution (Operation Flood) in India was aimed at increasing:
mcq.explain: Operation Flood, launched in 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board under Dr Verghese Kurien, built a nationwide milk grid linking producers' cooperatives to consumers. It made India one of the world's largest milk producers. The Green Revolution related to food grains, especially wheat.
mcq.topic: Post-independence strategy (1947–1991): planning, public sector, licence raj

mcq.q: Which statement about the reforms of the 1980s is correct?
options: They fully dismantled industrial licensing for all industries
Some controls were relaxed and growth improved, but the reforms were partial and not a comprehensive change of policy
They led to the creation of NITI Aayog
mcq.explain: In the 1980s, governments relaxed some industrial and import controls, encouraged technology upgradation and allowed broad-banding of licences, and growth improved. But these steps were piecemeal, which is why they are sometimes called "reforms by stealth". Comprehensive delicensing came only in 1991, GST in 2017 and NITI Aayog in 2015.
mcq.topic: Early liberalisation in the 1980s ("reforms by stealth")

mcq.q: The First Five Year Plan (1951–56) gave the highest priority to:
options: Agriculture, including irrigation and power projects
mcq.explain: The First Plan, launched in 1951, focused on agriculture, irrigation and power, because food shortages and the effects of Partition were urgent problems. It largely achieved its targets. The Second Plan (1956–61) then shifted the emphasis to heavy and basic industries under the Mahalanobis model.
mcq.topic: Post-independence strategy (1947–1991): planning, public sector, licence raj
mcq.fast: First Plan = agriculture; Second Plan = heavy industry.

mcq.q: The Planning Commission of India was set up in the year:
mcq.explain: The Planning Commission was set up by a resolution of the Government of India in March 1950, with the Prime Minister as its Chairman, to formulate Five Year Plans. The First Plan began in 1951. The Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015.
mcq.topic: Post-independence strategy (1947–1991): planning, public sector, licence raj
mcq.fast: Planning Commission 1950 -> First Plan 1951 -> NITI Aayog 2015.

mcq.q: The economic crisis that triggered the 1991 reforms was mainly a:
options: Stock market bubble in technology shares
Balance of payments crisis, with foreign exchange reserves falling to very low levels
Banking crisis caused by sub-prime housing loans
mcq.explain: By mid-1991, India faced a severe balance of payments crisis: foreign exchange reserves had fallen to a level sufficient for only a few weeks of imports, the fiscal deficit was high and inflation was rising. The government responded with stabilisation measures and structural reforms. Sub-prime loans relate to the 2008 US crisis.
mcq.topic: The 1991 crisis and the reform package (LPG)

mcq.q: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, launched in 2014, mainly aims at:
options: Financial inclusion by providing bank accounts to households without them
mcq.explain: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, launched in August 2014, aims at universal access to banking through basic savings accounts, along with RuPay debit cards, accident insurance and access to credit and pensions. These accounts also became channels for direct benefit transfers of subsidies.
mcq.topic: Outcomes of three decades of reform
mcq.fast: Jan Dhan = bank accounts for all (financial inclusion).
